title: Pierron's band at Spanish Fort
summary: Rau describes Spanish Fort and Pierron's band, a quiet, well-timed New Orleans jazz group of violin, guitar and piano where people danced.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you ever go to Trancinas?

Well, this was what they used to call Trancinas in those days. It was at Spanish Fort and Pierron's band was the one that was famous there for many years. We'd go out there, we'd take a streetcar, I remember in those days. You'd get on a streetcar at Canal Street and go all the way out to Spanish Fort. That band used to be playing out there in those days.
Was that band playing what you would call jazz as opposed to what you used to hear and you used to hear?

It was New Orleans jazz, but it wasn't loud music. Pierron was a violinist and he had guitar playing, they had Sweet Ammo playing the piano and two or three others in there. I don't think they had any brass instruments in there. They probably had a couple of saxophones or something like that. But it was pretty music. I mean, he was well known. They had wonderful timing. Everybody used to love to go out there to dance. And when they went out there, they danced. It was just a place that people would go to. It had a vogue for a few years. And that was the place to go. Later on, it was the West End Roof. That was when your father and Red and that bunch, I quit by then. Yeah, that's right.
